_about.purpose: Phase 11 evaluation query set. SILVER (provisional) labels — authored by the project, not yet expert-validated. Numbers computed against it must be reported as preliminary until Dr. Sunita T. Pandey / the expert gold-set replaces or ratifies these labels.
_about.labelling: Two levels. BOOK level (available now): `relevant_books` marks which treatise(s) plausibly address the condition — supports Precision@k, nDCG, MRR, Hit@k. PASSAGE level (added later): `relevant_chunk_ids`, once populated, additionally makes Recall@k well-defined, since only then is the true number of relevant passages known.
_about.query_style: Queries are SYMPTOM-led, not crop-led, because the classical texts are general and symptom-based rather than crop-indexed. The crop is recorded separately as context only.
_about.coverage_relabel_2026_09_15: expect_answerable was originally true for all 22 non-negative queries — an ASSUMPTION, never verified against the corpus. Coverage check (§6m, scripts/check_coverage.py) scored every query with the pipeline's own cross-encoder: 4 strong (>=0.35), 5 marginal (0.15-0.35), 13 no match (<0.15). The 13 are now expect_answerable=false with the score recorded. Over-refusal must be reported on the answerable subset; the original file is preserved as silver_queries.pre_coverage.json. This is a finding, not a patch: it quantifies the gap between classical IKS aetiology and modern lesion-based disease labels.
_about.extension_2026_09_26: Extended with 16 domain-derived queries covering pest damage, soil, seed treatment, season, water, planting and physical injury — the subject areas these treatises actually cover. The original 22 queries were almost entirely modern fungal leaf diseases, which §6m showed the texts cannot address, so the evaluation was measuring the system against unanswerable questions. Candidates were written from the domain WITHOUT consulting the corpus (to avoid circularity), then labelled from measured cross-encoder scores: 8 strong, 7 marginal, 1 no-coverage. Queries scoring 'none' were kept as honest negatives, not deleted.
_about.provisional_disease_labels: 11 disease queries marked no_coverage carry label_provisional=true. Their labels were assigned from hand-written query wording, but the deployed pipeline uses Strategy B's wording instead. Stage 0 (6o) measures Llama's real queries; if Llama scores higher, these labels are re-derived from that. The 16 domain queries added 2026-09-26 are NOT affected - they have no disease label and are never produced by the vision pipeline.
_about.generated_query_field: 17 disease queries carry generated_query: the query Strategy B (Llama) actually produces from that disease label, recorded 2026-09-26 after the prompt fix (6o, Stage 3 round 2). The deployed system never uses the authored `query` field for these - it only ever sends what the bridge writes - so an evaluation of the real system must use generated_query. The authored wording is retained as a comparison ceiling. Load with load_query_set(query_source='generated') to evaluate the deployed system, or 'authored' (default) for the ceiling. The 23 domain queries and the 2 negative controls have no generated form: the vision pipeline cannot produce them, so they keep their authored wording under either setting.
_about.relevant_books_relabel_2026_09_26: The 16 domain queries added on 2026-09-26 initially took relevant_books from the top-3 books of their own retrieval run, which made Precision@5, nDCG and MRR circular - retrieval graded against its own output. Symptom: keyword_only P@5 rose 0.33 -> 0.53 purely from adding queries. They are now labelled from each treatise's subject matter, the same basis as the original 24, with the reason recorded per query in relevant_books_basis. Author-assigned, pending expert ratification. Generation metrics were never affected: they use expect_answerable and citation resolution, never relevant_books.
